title: Unity of type reflects a common progenitor's pattern modified by slight steps

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Unity of type reflects a common progenitor's pattern modified by slight steps

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The shared pattern of homologous organs within a class is explained by descent from an ancient progenitor (an archetype) that already had that pattern, which natural selection then modified by slight successive steps for different uses without transposing parts.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: If we suppose that the ancient progenitor, the archetype as it may be called, of all mammals, had its limbs constructed on the existing general pattern, for whatever purpose they served, we can at once perceive the plain signification of the homologous construction of the limbs throughout the whole class.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIII, “Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs”; section “MORPHOLOGY, between members of the same class, between parts of the same individual”. Scope: members of the same class (e.g. mammal limbs, insect mouthparts)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch13-14: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Common ancestry of homologous patterns and transformation sequences are strongly testable with independent molecular and fossil data. Attribution of every step to natural selection is less discriminating, but the central historical inference is resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct ancestral anatomical patterns from independent phylogenies and comparative morphology, then test whether homologous organs are parsimoniously derived by successive modifications without topological transposition. Concordant ancestral patterns and graded transformations support the account.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Ancestral states are inferred rather than directly observed.

Gradual and selection-driven modification can be difficult to separate from other evolutionary mechanisms.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Presence of the shared pattern in stem fossils is testable, and public matrices and occurrences support it for mammal limbs and a few other systems. 'Slight successive steps' and the ancestral function are much harder, and reconstruction methods favor the gradual story they are asked to detect. The feasible result is a partial historical test for well-fossilized organ systems, not for every class.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct the ancestral arrangement of a class-level organ system from fossils and living species, and test whether subsequent changes are small steps in shape and size that leave connections intact. The claim is confirmed if stem fossils already show the shared pattern and later disparity accumulates gradually, and refuted if the common ancestor lacks the pattern or later change is concentrated in a few large jumps.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fine stratigraphic series of slight steps are available for a few skeletonized lineages and missing for most organ systems.

Ancestral-state models assume a tree and a mode of change, so gradual modification is partly built into the method.

The original use of the ancestral pattern is not recorded by the fossils that preserve its structure.
